rule: Eliran Shopen, 2026-11-05: «סטייה נורמלית זה גג עד 2%», then «גם סטייה של 2% זה הרבה, אני רוצה להוריד את אחוז הסטייה למינימלי», and «אם יש סטייה מעל 2% אני גם לא רוצה שתבטל את ההדמייה אלא תעשה הכל כדי שהכל יהיה תקין והכל יופיע כמו בתכנית מכר». A room over max_deviation_pct is NEVER dropped or hidden: the gate's FAIL starts the fix loop, and the package refuses only while a room still fails.

parameters.max_deviation_pct: the per-room bar: PASS only when deviation_pct <= this AND the gate can resolve it in that room (resolution_pct <= this); the disclosure line carries this same number
parameters.min_finding_deg: the narrowest run of failing columns that counts as a finding: 0.35 deg = ONE column at 1024 (so that 1% is resolvable in the dining room, whose walls are far); runs narrower than strong_gap_below_deg count only with a gap >= 2x delta, against the depth model's own noise
parameters.max_attempts: the fix loop's limit per room before it reports to Eliran; it never ships without the room. 5 since 2026-11-05 (the coordinator: the portal's acceptance run on apt846 needed band repairs beyond 3 — attempt 1 the skin, 2 a regeneration, 3..5 CG-guided band repairs)

fix_loop: 1. fidelity-gate FAIL on a room -> attempt 1: regenerate the skin with the CG render as Image 1 (gen-pano, the room's skin-prompts entry) and gate again
2. still FAIL -> attempts 2..max_attempts: CG-guided band repairs at the flagged bearings (close-seam --u <bearing u> --band-deg <width> --extra 'inside the band follow Image 2 ...'), each gated
3. past max_attempts -> stop and report the room's numbers to Eliran; the room is never shipped silently and never dropped: build-tour refuses to package until it passes
4. a deviation the trace itself carries (trace vs the plan's printed dimensions, UNRESOLVED rows) is fixed in the trace and the CG re-rendered, not in the skin

consistency_judge.rule: The coordinator's ruling 2026-11-05 (option a, reported to Eliran): the vision judge disagrees with itself on unchanged pictures (apt846 bedroom-main: 3 PASS of 5 on the same 07/08 pair; fork B measured judge agreement 0.5-0.67). A group's verdict is the MAJORITY of 3 runs on unchanged pictures; a picture changed between runs restarts the count.

consistency_judge.render_rule: R27 (the coordinator's ruling 2026-11-06): each photo is judged beside its OWN final render from the same viewpoint (apartment.json sets.original.cg_tour); the judge reports only differences the renders do not explain (furniture, materials, colours, fixtures, and architecture that departs from its own render). View-dependent architecture (a square corner with a doorway from the entrance, the rounded end from the living room) is not an inconsistency. Not a weaker judge: a photo that departs from its own render is still reported.

band_edge.rule: R25 (2026-11-05, the coordinator's order after Eliran found a visible cut in the LIVE 02-kitchen): no visible band edge ships. close-seam v3 (tools/band_blend.py) records per cut the structure left where the repaint meets the picture (<picture>.seam.json); fidelity-gate FAILS a picture whose repair chain has a cut above max_structure, or a v1/v2 composite (no readable cut) not listed in eye_cleared. Calibrated on apt846 crops 2026-11-05: visible cuts measured 5.4-12.1 (a sofa split, a doubled TV, an armchair cut, a counter step at 5.73); clean cuts 1.2-4.7. R25b (the coordinator, 2026-11-05 late, after a 12-px skirting step scored 1.8 on structure): at each cut every near-horizontal line both pictures carry (skirting, counter edge, shelf, wall-ceiling line) is matched between the picture and the repaint (normalised correlation >= 0.7); a step >= max_line_step_px FAILS. Calibrated: the skirting step 5 px, clean cuts 0-3 px.

ref_scale.rule: R28 (the coordinator's ruling 2026-11-06, after fork F found a --ref repair transplanting the reference's close-up at the wrong scale while the depth gate passed it at 0.19%): (a) every --ref band repair: the object's apparent width AFTER the repair vs BEFORE it (the same picture), +-10% (close-seam runs it after every --ref repair and writes it into the sidecar; band-lineage fails a --ref band without its PASS); (b) built-in, plan-dimensioned elements (kitchen run/column, wardrobes, vanities) vs the final render: +-15%; (c) loose furniture vs the final render: +-25%, with the R27 judge. Calibrated 2026-11-06: designed loose furniture runs 10-16% wider than the render's placeholder blocks; boxes are ~10% noisy.
ref_scale.near_camera_rule: A camera-to-object distance under ~1.5 m uses the 1% depth gate as the authority: at that range the box widths of a vision call exaggerate (perspective, the object cut by the frame), so an R28 ratio there is reported, not enforced (the coordinator's ruling 2026-11-06).

consistency_checklist.rule: R31 + R32 (2026-11-06, the coordinator after Eliran found on the LIVE tour 04-living's kitchen with upper cabinets, a straight run and no stainless while 02/03 show open curved shelves on stainless — the R27 judge passed that group 3/3 — and 02's sink seemingly beside the fridge). The consistency verdict is deterministic code over fixed fields, never the judge's free text: (R32) per view the judge fills the group's checklist; every field must agree across the views that see it and match what the data expects (plan-derived defaults + apartments/<id>/consistency-expect.json); any mismatch = FAIL; (R31) the hob, sink and tall column positions become along-run offsets in cm and the gaps are checked against the plan's. judge.same and differences are kept as notes only.

spacing.note: x → bearing → the ray meets the run line (the sink's counter, its longest edge) through the fixture's plan point; the along-run gap between two fixtures vs the plan's. Hand measurement noise on the 2026-11-06 kitchen views was about ±15-20 cm, hence ±30. A ray within 20° of the run line is skipped. Each pair's tolerance = tol_cm + the along-run shift a ±bearing_noise_deg misreading of x causes for both fixtures (root-sum-square), so a far, oblique view gets a wider band and a near, square view a tight one.

upper_cabinets.ask: closed upper wall cabinets (cupboards with doors) mounted on the wall above the worktop anywhere on the run

shelves_open.ask: open shelves (no doors) on the wall above the worktop

shelves_shape.ask: the open shelves' shape seen from above: curved (rounded or curved ends/fronts) or straight; none when there are no open shelves

backsplash.ask: the wall finish between the worktop and whatever is above it

tall_type.ask: what the tall column visibly IS: fridge (full-height flush doors, a fridge-freezer), oven (built-in ovens at eye height), storage (plain doors, no appliance)

tall_front.ask: the tall column's fronts: the same lacquer panels as the run's base fronts, stainless steel, glass, or other

oven_visible.ask: a built-in oven front (a dark glass door with a handle or a control strip) is visible anywhere in the kitchen

oven_where.ask: where that oven is: directly under the hob, in the tall column, elsewhere, or none when no oven is visible

sink_fridge_gap_units.ask: how many base-cabinet fronts (a door or a drawer stack, each about 60 cm wide) lie between the sink bowl and the tall column; 0 = the sink is right next to the column; null when the sink or the column is not visible
